name: QR payment made without verifying the payee's banking name
description: CERT-In directs users to verify the payee's registered banking name before paying by QR. Well evidenced, and unobservable: TrustLens sees a submitted artifact after the fact, not the live payment flow. Retained as knowledge against a future device-side or payment-integrated component.

source_references.quote: Verify the sender's banking name before making payments using QR codes.

explanation.plain: Before paying any QR code, check that the name shown is the person or business you mean to pay.
explanation.technical: Deferred, not weak. The evidence is a verified CERT-In instruction; what is missing is the observation point — TrustLens is not inside the payment flow and cannot see whether the payee name was checked (CONF-003, NG-05).
explanation.why_confidence_limited: TrustLens can observe that a QR and a payment context are present in submitted content. It cannot observe the user's verification behaviour, which is the actual subject of the rule.

provenance.notes: Demonstrates that evidence and implementability are independent filters: this rule is better evidenced than several published ones and still cannot run. | WP3/G-07: globally-scoped suppressors removed from suppressed_by (now auto-applied from negative-indicator-library-v1.json); only family-specific guards remain.
